svg.text: Figure 6-1 · The SOTIF line-up: from each hazard to its evidence
Per SOTIF hazard: what exposes it, what changes the function, and what must be shown before the residual risk is accepted
Model-commanded steering moves the vehicle out of the
Lateral control insufficient for the road
Driver override not recognised or not effective as the
Stock PCS performance degraded by the item's intended
Assisted lane change into an occupied lane
No reaction to a VRU in or entering the path
System stays engaged outside the ODD
Apply to every hazard and not repeated per row: validation targets VT-09, VT-10, VT-11; acceptance criteria AC-01, AC-07.
A row shows what the documents link, not what is done: no modification is verified and no validation target is frozen or met yet. SH-07 is not used (WP-C-05 §2).

g.text: Terms: AC-nn acceptance criterion (WP-C-05 §5.3) · C0–C3 controllability class C0 (controllable in general) to C3 (difficult or uncontrollable) · FI-nn functional insufficiency (WP-C-06) · FM-nn functional

modification (WP-C-07) · G0–G6 gate G0…G6 of the project lifecycle · ODD operational design domain: where the system is meant to work · P1–P3 priority of a functional modification: P1 before on-road use, P2 before

release, P3 decide at G2 · PCS pre-collision system: Toyota's stock collision warning and braking · S0–S3 severity class S0 (no injuries) to S3 (life-threatening) · SH-nn SOTIF hazard (WP-C-05) · SOTIF safety of the

intended functionality (ISO 21448): hazards with nothing failing · TC-nn triggering condition (WP-C-06) · VRU vulnerable road user: pedestrian or cyclist · VT-nn validation target (WP-V-02) · WP-nn work product,
e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its area (M management, C concept, S system, H hardware, W software, V validation, P processes, A analyses, O operation, K safety case)
